passages.original: Vt te Virgilium saecula nostra darent.
passages.english: So that our ages might give you [to us as] a Virgil.
passages.notes: Isolated line, probably the second line of an elegiac couplet; the purpose clause depends on a preceding line not given. The sense is likely 'that our age might produce you as a [new] Virgil'.

passages.original: Transit ad Ambrosium: plus fauet ira deae.
passages.english: It passes over to Ambrose: the goddess's anger favours [him] more.
passages.notes: Isolated pentameter without context; the subject of 'transit' and the identity of the goddess are unclear. 'plus favet ira deae' might also be understood as 'the goddess's wrath is more favourable'. Ambrose is unidentified.
